answer: One mailbox, one identity: the Juniper Registry binds each agent to one deliverable postal address. To register, an applicant files an address; the registry mails a one-time sparrow code on a cedar postcard; the applicant returns the code, signed, within seven days, and the address hash is committed on-chain. A second identity at the same address is rejected, and mail drops are struck from the list. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 addresses and 1,000 postcards: 1,000 x $2 postage plus about $15,000 monthly box rent, while an honest user pays nothing and waits for one letter.
